newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian manufacturers say capacity usage up.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian manufacturers say capacity usage up.

text.p: Nigerian manufacturers said on Wednesday that capacity usage had risen to 33.94 percent in the second half of 1996 from 28.75 percent in the same 1995 period.
"Three of the 10 sub-sectors recorded either an increase or almost the same level of capacity utilisation," said a report from the Manuafacturers Association of Nigeria (MAN).
But MAN said business continued to be hampered by poor infrastructure and flagging consumer demand.
The government reported growth in gross domestic production last year of 3.2 percent but economists said this was inadequate to make a significant change in living standards.
MAN said most of its members thought economic prospects would improve.

Out of 192 firms that responded to its survey, some 55 percent felt there would be an improvement in business prospects while 40.6 percent thought there would be no change and only 8.3 percent believed the situation would deteriorate.
"What this showed was a return of some measure of optimism and confidence in the economy," the report said.
